### 📝 Description

<!--
Describe the Chore.

In software engineering, a "chore" is a task that must be done to maintain the health and integrity of the codebase but doesn't necessarily result in observable changes or direct value to the user.

Chores are usually internal tasks that keep the development process running smoothly and efficiently. They help to ensure the quality, maintainability, and scalability of the system.

Examples of chores might include:

- Refactoring code for better readability or performance.
- Writing or updating technical documentation.
- Configuring or updating build systems, linters, or other tools used in the development process.
- Removing obsolete code or dependencies.
- Improving test coverage or writing new tests for existing code.

Chores are a crucial part of software development because they help maintain a healthy codebase and an efficient development environment, making it easier and quicker to add new features and fix bugs. They are typically tracked and prioritized alongside other work items, like new features and bug fixes.
-->
